questions.q: What is a freeze window, and why is it necessary for cutover?
options: A period after go-live when users can't log in, to let the system stabilize
The time during rehearsal when a sandbox is refreshed
A period when Salesforce automatically locks all validation rules
A defined period during which the legacy system stops accepting changes, so the final migration load works against a stable, unmoving source
questions.explain: Without a freeze, the final extract is a snapshot of a constantly changing system — records created or edited after the extract was taken would never make it into the migration at all.

questions.q: Where should a freeze window's planned length actually come from?
options: An optimistic guess made before any load has ever been timed
The actual load duration measured during rehearsal, with some margin
The business's preferred lunch-hour schedule, regardless of load duration
A fixed, universal duration used identically for every migration project
questions.explain: The freeze window has to be informed directly by the rehearsal's measured load duration (Lesson 14) plus margin — not an estimate made before anyone actually timed the real load.

questions.q: What is a "delta record" in the context of cutover?
options: A record created or changed during the freeze window, after the main extract was taken
A record that failed validation during the main load
A record that was deliberately excluded from migration scope
A record that only exists in a Partial Copy sandbox
questions.explain: A delta record is one created or modified during the freeze window after the main extract — the cutover plan has to explicitly decide how these get handled, whether via a planned delta load or manual re-entry.

questions.q: What is the purpose of deciding a go/no-go checklist in advance, rather than evaluating conditions in the moment on cutover day?
options: It has no real purpose beyond formality
It replaces the need for a cutover runbook entirely
It prevents the team from waving through a "probably fine" item under cutover-day pressure that wouldn't have passed calm scrutiny earlier
It is only required for phased migrations, not big-bang ones
questions.explain: Deciding the go/no-go conditions ahead of time, when there's no time pressure, prevents the team from rationalizing a weak 'probably fine' judgment call during the high-pressure cutover event itself.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say communicating the freeze window to the business is part of the plan, not just a courtesy?
options: Because Salesforce enforces freeze windows automatically once scheduled
Because communication is only needed after cutover is complete
Because the runbook cannot be written until communication is finished
Because a freeze window the business doesn't actually observe, due to not being told, effectively didn't happen regardless of how well it was planned on paper
questions.explain: A freeze window only works if the people who would otherwise keep using the legacy system actually know to stop — without that communication, the freeze is undermined no matter how carefully it was designed.
